mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS is low and UNRATE is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS in a tightening cycle leads to higher borrowing costs, reducing corporate profitability and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High CPIAUCSL indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as costs rise.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL is high but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production is below 100 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment but decreasing retail sales indicates consumer weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Employment rises and retail sales fall but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates a weak housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts are low but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 40% of cases.
